statement: A particle is projected vertically upward with initial speed $u = 40\text{ m/s}$ from ground level. Taking $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$, at what time in seconds is its height $y = 60\text{ m}$ above the ground?
solution: Ambiguous numerical target: The equation $y = u t - \frac{1}{2} g t^2 \implies 5 t^2 - 40 t + 60 = 0 \implies t^2 - 8 t + 12 = 0$ yields two distinct physical solutions: $t_1 = 2.0\text{ s}$ (ascending) and $t_2 = 6.0\text{ s}$ (descending). Because the question omits whether the ascending or descending instant is sought, both $2.0\text{ s}$ and $6.0\text{ s}$ are valid answers.
assumptions: ADVERSARIAL_FIXTURE: Multiple valid positive real roots without physical discriminator
intended_learning_objective: Test ambiguity gate detection of multiple valid numerical answers
